text:
maria: Heads up — saw a ~15% tail latency regression on long-seq (L=2048) benchmarks after yesterday's batcher heuristics roll. nvtx timelines show a memcopy spike during KV warmup.
ajay: Ack. Can you paste the nsys command and a short timeline snippet?
maria: Sure — ran on a perf node:```bash
nsys profile --output=run1 --trace=cuda,nvtx,osrt --sample=cpu -t 60 \
  --capture-range=nvtx:span --env "CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0" \
  ./bench_longseq --seq_len=2048 --workload=kv-cache --iters=200
```
maria: timeline excerpt (nvtx spans):```text
[         ] kernel: cublasLtMatmul        120ms
[         ] kernel: kv_prefetch_kernel     30ms
[         ] memcpy: cudaMemcpyAsync H2D    95ms  <-- unexpected spike
[         ] kernel: attention_mask          25ms
```
perfbot: perfbot: uploaded profile artifact: https://perf.company.internal/runs/3987654321
julia: That cudaMemcpyAsync jump during warmup smells like a prefetch window change. Any config diffs pushed yesterday?
kevin: I rolled the batcher heuristic that increases prefetch_window from 16 -> 32 for longer sequences to reduce stalls. It was in commit 7f3a2d4 (batcher: aggressive prefetch for long sequences).
ajay: Good lead. If prefetch window doubled, KV prefetch could be issuing larger host->device transfers more frequently, shifting overlap and causing memcpy to serialize with GEMM kernels.
maria: I compared before/after flamegraphs — before the commit, memcpy was mostly overlapped and tiny; after it grows and sits on the critical path. Quick diff:```text
before: tokens/sec=420 ± 3, memcpy tail ~10ms
after:  tokens/sec=355 ± 5, memcpy tail ~95ms
```
julia: Can we reproduce with a minimal repro and bisect the commit range? Suggest doing `git bisect start -- bad=HEAD good=origin/main~10` and run the bench script that hits the prefetch path.
ajay: I'll start a bisect job with a deterministic seed and the same node image. Bisect script:```bash
#!/bin/bash
git bisect run ./tools/bisect_helper.sh --bench=bench_longseq --seq_len=2048 --iters=50
```
kevin: Also try toggling `prefetch_window=16` back on the after-commit binary to see if behavior reverts (cheap check before full bisect).
maria: I ran that quick toggle (recompiled with window=16) — latency returned to baseline in my local run. So it's likely the heuristic tweak.
ajay: Bisect step 1/15: testing 7d1c9 -> result: good (no memcpy spike). Step 2/15: testing 7f3a2d4 -> result: bad (memcpy spike). Looks like 7f3a2d4 is the culprit.
julia: Great, next: can we make prefetch issue smaller transfers or ensure async copies don't block kernels? Maybe use `cudaMemcpyAsync` with different stream placement or chunking.
kevin: I'll open an RFC to change prefetch to chunked transfers with max_chunk_bytes = 4MB and also add an opt-out flag for aggressive prefetch.
maria: For the incident notes: bisect found commit 7f3a2d4; root cause: doubling prefetch window causing larger H2D async transfers that end up serialized on our stream and increase kernel scheduling pressure. Mitigation: revert or chunked-copy + stream separation.
perfbot: perfbot: bisect job completed: https://perf.company.internal/bisect/3987654321 (logs + nsys artifacts attached)
ajay: I'll run a follow-up nsys with stream-separation patch to validate (expect memcpy overlapped and tokens/sec back up).
kevin: Thanks — plan: ship small patch that chunks prefetch and add telemetry around memcpy tail, then rollback heuristic if telemetry shows regression in prod.
maria: Sounds good. @everyone please add any extra repro details to the bisect ticket.
ajay: on it :+1:
maria: thx all.
